sentences.text: This appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 challenging the judgment and award dated 16.04.2019 passed in MVC No.577/2018 by the Court of the Prl.
Senior Civil Judge and J.M.F.C. at Pandavapura (hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal').

2. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.2- Insurance Company.
3.
The status of the parties before the Tribunal is retained for the sake of convenience.

The case of the appellant/claimant is that he filed a claim petition before the Tribunal under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act (for short 'M.V. Act') claiming compensation of Rs.19,50,000/-
for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 09.12.2017.

It is alleged that on the said date when the petitioner was proceeding on the road near Vanajasundar Coultry, at that time, a bike bearing No.KA-11-EC-7656 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the petitioner, due to which, he has sustained injuries and he was admitted in the hospital for nine days.
He was an agriculturist and also working in hotel.
Due to the accidental injuries, he was suffering from disability.
Therefore, the claimant filed the petition seeking compensation on various grounds.

5. Respondent No.2-Insurance Company appeared before the Tribunal and filed written statement and denied the petition averments and also disputed the manner of accident, age of injuries,
occupation including NC: 2024:KHC:21372 the income and disability suffered by the petitioner and prayed for dismissal of the suit.

6. On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed the following issues for consideration:

sentences.text:
Whether the Petitioner proves that on 09.12.2017 at about 10.30 a.m. when the petitioner went along with his aunt's son by name Raghu to purchase a cow were going from Harahalli towards Kennalu Village by walk on the left side of the road near Vanaja-Sundar Kalyana Mantap on Pandavapura-Mysore main road, at that time, a bike bearing Reg.No.KA- 11/EC-7656 came from Pandavapura side being ridden by its rider in a very rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life came from back side and dashed against the petitioner, due to which, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries as alleged in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner further proves that the said accident was due to negligence on the part of rider of bike bearing Reg.No.KA-11/EC- 7656?
3. Whether the 2nd respondent proves that the rider of the bike bearing Reg.No.KA-11/EC- 7656 was not holding valid and effective NC: 2024:KHC:21372 driving licenses to ride particular class of vehicle as on the date of the accident?
4. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, from whom and to what extent?
5. What order or award?
7. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1, the doctor was examined as PW.2 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P38.
The respondents have not led any evidence.

8. On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both parties, the tribunal answered issue No.1 in the affirmative, issue Nos.2 and 3 in the negative, issue No.4 partly in the affirmative and the tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.3,14,967/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization and also held respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the claimant and directed to NC: 2024:KHC:21372 deposit the compensation amount within a period of thirty days from the date of award.
9. Being aggrieved by the meager compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant is before this Court challenging the impugned judgment and award.

10. It is the vehement contention of the learned counsel for appellant-claimant that the Tribunal has committed an error in considering the income of the petitioner as Rs.9,000/- p.m., even though the petitioner was earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Even in the Lok-adalath chart, for the accident was occurred in the year 2017, Rs.11,000/- p.m. is considered as notional income.

Apart from that the tribunal awarded meager amount towards 'pain and suffering', 'future medical expenses', 'food,
died, nourishment, conveyance and other incidental charges', 'loss of amenities', 'loss of income during treatment period' and same has to be enhanced.

He further contended that the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner for a sum of Rs.1,20,214/-, the tribunal left out one '0' and C S Mahendra vs R C Somakumara on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86367903/
3 awarded NC: 2024:KHC:21372 only Rs.12,214/-.

sentences.text: Hence, he seeks enhancement of compensation and prays to allow the appeal.
11. Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent- Insurance Company justified the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
However, he fairly admits that Rs.11,000/- could be considered as notional income of the petitioner.
Therefore, on these grounds, he seeks dismissal of the appeal.

12. Having heard the learned counsel for appellant- claimant and the learned counsel for respondent-Insurance Company, on perusal of the Exs.P1 to P38, the point to be considered is as to whether the tribunal has committed an error in awarding meager compensation in respect of 'pain and suffering' considering the necessary income awarding in respect of medical expenses, income during laid up treatment, etc., which requires to be enhanced?

13. On perusal of the records, the accident was occurred on 09.12.2017 at about 10.30 a.m., is not NC: 2024:KHC:21372 disputed, due to which, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he was admitted in the hospital for nine days as an inpatient and he has suffered fracture of right knee and left wrist.

The doctor has opinioned that he has undergone surgery in the hospital and suffered disability to an extent of 34.11% to the whole body, such being the case, he was suffering from fracture of injuries on the lower limb awarding 11.37% is meager and the same is enhancing to 50%
instead of 11.37% awarded by the tribunal.
14.

As regards the medical expenses, the petitioner produced the documents of medical records and calculation memo of Rs.1,20,213.28 as per para No.22 of the judgment, but the tribunal left out one '0' and considered only Rs.12,213.28 instead of Rs.1,20,213.28.

Hence, Rs.1,20,214/- has to be considered as 'medical expenses'.
15.
As regards 'the pain and suffering', the tribunal awarded Rs.50,000/- is retained.

With regard to 'food, diet, nourishment, conveyance and other incidental charges', the tribunal awarded a compensation of Rs.25,000/- which is just and proper and the same remains unaltered.
17.
As regards 'the loss of income during treatment period', the tribunal considered only for one month is incorrect.

Hence, it should be calculated for two months and it would comes to Rs.11,000/-
X 2 = 22,000/-.
18.
As regards 'the future medical expenses', the tribunal awarded a compensation of Rs.20,000/- is meager.
Hence, I propose to award Rs.30,000/- towards 'the future medical expenses' instead of Rs.20,000/- awarded by the tribunal.

19. As regards 'the loss of amenities', the tribunal erred in considering the disability at 11.37% to the whole body, such being the case, Rs.10,000/- awarded by the tribunal towards 'the loss of amentias'
is a meager amount.

Hence, I propose to award Rs.20,000/- towards C S Mahendra vs R C Somakumara on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86367903/
4 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:21372 'the loss of amenities' instead of Rs.10,000/- awarded by the tribunal.

X 12 X 17 X 11.37% = Rs.2,55,142.8/, which is rounded off to Rs.2,55,143/-.
